artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
Transience is a compilation album by Steven Wilson, released in 2015 on the Kscope label. It features a curated selection of 13 tracks recorded between 2003 and 2015, showcasing the more accessible and melodic side of Wilson’s solo work. The album spans over an hour and includes a new 2015 studio version of "Lazarus," originally a Porcupine Tree song, alongside edited versions of tracks from his solo albums. Musically, it blends progressive rock with elements of post-progressive and art rock, emphasizing atmospheric textures, intricate arrangements, and Wilson’s multi-instrumental talents.

Positioned as an introduction to Wilson’s solo career, Transience distills his expansive and often complex output into a more approachable format, making it a significant entry point for new listeners. The release was initially a limited edition vinyl pressing, notable for its lavish gatefold sleeve and etched fourth side, which contributed to its appeal among collectors. Commercially, the album performed well, reaching #3 on the UK vinyl charts, reflecting Wilson’s growing prominence in the progressive rock scene. Critically, it was well received for its coherent flow and the quality of the selected tracks, with Classic Rock magazine awarding it 8/10 and recommending it as a strong starting point for those unfamiliar with his work.
